---
title: "Apps native Start on Vite+ and Cloudflare"
description: "Qualify native Apps SSR and its exact emitted artifact before staging or canonical promotion."
updatedAt: "2026-11-01"
audience: developers
---

Apps has a native Start SSR candidate with the production catalogue, existing
satellite providers, English/Vietnamese locale behavior, build-info and guarded
central API forwarding. Registered public redirects run at the Worker Request
URL boundary; the Router does not serialize their query strings. Cards and the
native navigation adapter use document navigation. The retained portable gateway
is predecessor source and cannot substitute for native acceptance.

The request context, `next/*` ports (document-mode navigation), `next-intl`
alias, Vite preset and central API forwarding come from
[`@tuturuuu/start-bridge`](/build/devops/start-bridge). `start-bridge.routes.json`
maps each retained App Router file to the native module that owns it, and CI
fails on any unmapped `route.*` or `page.*`.

## Owning validation

`.github/workflows/apps-cloudflare.yaml` uses Bun 1.4.4 and Node 24.22.0. Root
Vitest, coverage and the Vitest override are pinned to 5.0.5; Apps pins Vite+
and its Vite alias to 1.3.0. The owning job builds
active dependencies, generates the exact checkout's build metadata, runs native
unit/types/lint and invokes `build:cloudflare` once for the frontend. The official
Void SDK supplies the Cloudflare adapter; no separate adapter or RSC mode is added.
No local release build is implied by this runbook.

For cold local unit checks, restore with `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, then run
`ttr resources run -- bun run test` from `apps/apps`. The isolated unit config
selects workspace `bun` source exports in both client and SSR resolution;
missing dependency `dist` exports must not trigger a local dependency build.
This source-only check does not replace exact-commit CI or emitted acceptance.

Shared Query public types require a single compatible materialized supplier
identity. `@tuturuuu/hooks` declares React Query peer `^5.102.8` and exports
`queryOptions` consumed by Web's `useQuery`. Cold CI exposed incompatible
`QueryClient` private fields between 5.104.4 and 5.102.8 despite preservation of
all prior static dependency graph edges. Align Apps' requested React Query
5.102.8 and `use-intl` 4.14.4 with the qualified shared materialized versions
through the owning package manager. Keep this repair scoped to Apps rather than
use a global version bump, cast, or suppression. Static graph equality and a
frozen dry-run do not prove materialized peer compatibility. After dependency
changes, require cold CI for the exact commit and acceptance of its emitted
runtime. An intl context split is an inferred risk, not an observed failure:
Apps' bare `next-intl` alias can unify the provider.

The artifact helper discovers the actual config through
exactly one native `.wrangler/deploy/config.json` or Void-saved
`.void/preview-deploy-config.json`. Both runtime harnesses use the shared
`scripts/ci/apps-native-runtime-pointer.mjs` reader. Saved pointer bytes retain
the original `.wrangler/deploy` relative base; never create a replacement pointer.
Missing, duplicate, malformed, symlinked or escaping pointers fail closed.
The focused reader regression suite covers both layouts and rejection cases;
receipt/source-SHA validation remains mandatory at its existing CI and browser
boundaries. Both `configPath` and an explicitly empty
`auxiliaryWorkers` array are required. The config, Worker main and assets must
stay within the output tree; ASSETS must use `dist/client`, Worker-first routing
and no SPA fallback. Static robots/sitemap bytes must match the checked-out public
sources. Added resources, routes, accounts, environments, secret declarations,
unknown config fields and symlinks fail closed. A new adapter field needs review
against its actual emitter; do not relax the contract to get a green job.
Void 1.1.12's owning Cloudflare Vite plugin 1.64.0 unconditionally emits
`no_bundle: true` and one ESModule rule with exactly `**/*.js` and `**/*.mjs`.
The source-derived fixture includes those fields and the exact serialized empty
normalizer defaults. Producer `configPath`/`userConfigPath` metadata points to the
original `.void-wrangler.jsonc`; it is sealed information, never dereferenced on
restore. The deploy pointer and emitted main/assets paths have independent
containment checks. The fixture is not observed build output or runtime evidence.
The Apps emitted-config contract also requires `upload_source_maps` to be exactly
JSON `true`. This reviewed emitted normalizer value is not an authored Apps
setting or proof of retained-state provenance. The regressions in
`scripts/ci/apps-native-artifact.test.py` reject false, number 1, null, string and
object substitutes and unrelated fields, and check raw emitted config bytes
through sealing and restore. Artifact validation does not qualify source-map
upload, dry-run, hosted runtime or publication.

The checked name `<staging-worker>` is the candidate's source-declared
sandbox name. This check does not establish an existing hosted Worker, account,
route, binding, credential, rollback version or provisioning authority. Staging
keeps `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1`. The candidate returns HTTP 503 for the canonical host
unless the separately admitted canonical-host flag is enabled. Apps has no no-staging override.

Generated Worker binding declarations and their compatibility harness live in
runner temporary storage. They must not overwrite the checked-out app source.
The owning `type-check` and applicable exact-source shared CI gates remain required.

## Actual emitted acceptance

`cloudflare/native-built-worker.test.mjs` runs the emitted Worker with disposable
local auth/API fixtures through the owning Wrangler/Miniflare emitted-module
adapter. Every runtime Worker has an outbound deny service permitting only those
exact fixture endpoints. A second instance of the same compiled Worker exercises
its real API handler against an unadmitted origin and must receive 599 without
fixture forwarding; the primary HTTP/SSR/RPC suite must record zero unexpected
requests. No runtime commit-hash override is supplied. It covers bilingual
signed/anonymous SSR, the real
compiled loader RPC, build identity, all 30 registered redirects, guard/central
status/method/body/cookie behavior and multiple response cookies. It includes 120
query assertions: duplicate/interleaved/numeric names, `__proto__`, literal JSON,
`next`, tracking, empty/repeated `source`, encoded slash, spaces and literal plus.
The default `source=apps` is appended only when the name is absent.

`scripts/ci/apps-native-browser.runtime.mjs` opens the emitted configuration in
local workerd through the official Wrangler/Miniflare adapter and invokes the
frozen `verifyNativeBrowserNavigation` helper. The helper loads the real catalogue,
attaches each regression query to an actual card anchor and clicks it, checking
Worker 307 Location and final browser URL for all 30 destinations. Only external
destination HTML is fulfilled with a disposable fixture. Other browser/provider
egress is denied. Existing Web Playwright owns the browser driver; this does not
add an Apps dependency or change the lock. Its availability and Chromium setup
must pass in the exact source job. Both new and restored artifacts run this gate.

The qualified source baseline passed 9 HTTP/runtime groups and 6 browser groups
on both original and restored artifacts. Each artifact passed 120 redirect and
120 browser-anchor cases using finite fixtures. These results apply to that
source and artifact only. They do not qualify a later HEAD, hosted runtime,
canonical cutover, an exact Chromium binary hash, internal descendant-process
closure or historical failure causes.

The runtime filename is intentionally outside generic source-only test discovery;
no artifact-dependent suite may silently run or skip in a job that never builds
or restores the artifact. The Python artifact suite is source-only and explicitly
selected by the owning workflow.

## Seal and restore

`scripts/ci/apps-native-artifact.py` hashes the complete dist tree and deploy
redirect under the exact checkout SHA. Runtime acceptance and Wrangler dry-run
must leave those bytes unchanged. Packing copies only checked member bytes and
its receipt; it does not invoke a build or deploy.

A fresh restore job checks the same source SHA and frozen dependencies, downloads
the single archive and rejects duplicates, traversal, symlinks, nonregular files,
extra/missing paths, hash mismatches and archive size/count excess before admitting
output. It restores only dist and the deploy redirect into clean owned output.
The restored configuration, Wrangler dry-run, emitted HTTP/RPC suite and ordinary
browser-anchor suite must pass again, followed by a final full hash comparison.
A missing or skipped native/runtime/browser gate is not acceptance.

### Failed-job sealed source diagnostics

The owning Meet, Calendar and Apps jobs may retain a separate
`*-debug-sealed-source-<source-sha>-<run-id>-<attempt>` artifact for three days.
Retention requires job failure, a successful canonical seal, and a successful
verify/pack step. Build or canonical config/seal failure produces no debug archive.
Meet seals before emitted runtime startup; accepted packing still follows all
existing runtime and bundle gates and re-verifies the seal. Calendar and Apps
retain their existing seal and acceptance ordering.

Debug packing reuses the canonical receipt and external expected source SHA;
checkout HEAD must match. The receipt records immutable file hashes. Meet and
Calendar verify the packed archive after extraction against the same receipt;
Apps uses its canonical per-member verified pack command. The adjacent bounded
metadata records the expected source SHA, checkout HEAD, event SHA (`GITHUB_SHA`),
workflow source SHA (explicit `github.workflow_sha` step environment), event name
(`GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`), run and attempt, plus archive and receipt hashes. No resealing, rebuilding, normalization repair
or acceptance bypass is permitted. Changed bytes fail closed. The normal success
archives and restore jobs remain separate and never consume these debug names.

The retained payload is limited to the already approved normal artifact members
and receipt, plus that metadata. Config vars remain constrained by each canonical
validator: Meet public service URLs and secret names only, Calendar empty vars
and required secret names, Apps the noindex marker and no secret bindings.
Calendar and Apps build auth bindings are synthetic fixtures. Meet's build uses
fixtures on pull requests and existing public Supabase URL/publishable-key
bindings otherwise; this does not admit private credentials, raw environment
files, or additional config. If a new field introduces private data, retain only
a reviewed bounded manifest/hash/file graph instead of that data.

These are **DEBUG sealed source, NOT qualified release** artifacts. A retained
archive does not make a failing runtime gate pass, establish a compiled typed
module graph, or qualify deployment. An actual failed-run upload, download and
receipt verification remain separate execution evidence.

## Delivery remains separate

This workflow validates and retains artifacts; it has no publish job, provider
credential or automatic traffic switch. Preserve the current canonical Vercel
artifact and route. Before any staging write, the integration owner must obtain
current hosted account/Worker/domain/routes/bindings/secret-name and deployment
mapping, confirm the proposed sandbox is admitted, capture rollback artifacts and
approve the scoped staging plan. No new Worker/resource/provider is provisioned
by this preparation.

After exact-commit CI and staging acceptance, the owner must complete synthetic
SSO/session-refresh/MFA, workspace permission/visibility, bilingual hydration,
command launcher, theme, static font/design and telemetry/consent acceptance.
The ordinary-anchor helper does not certify all of those behaviors. Canonical
promotion requires its own target admission, rollback qualification and existing
release gates. Publish only the already qualified restored artifact through the
existing Wrangler path after one final hash check; ordinary Void CLI deployment
rebuilds/preflights and cannot stand in for exact-artifact publication. Do not
borrow Meet's no-staging exception or another SHA's success.
